extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent practitioners, and applicants evaluating subject-matter eligibility (SME), including AI-related inventions
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO SME analysis for patent claims
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applying the USPTO/MPEP subject-matter eligibility framework (Step 1, Step 2A Prongs One & Two, and Step 2B) to patent claims, with examples drawn from AI and biotech contexts. Focuses on identifying judicial exceptions (abstract ideas, laws of nature), assessing additional claim elements, and determining whether claims integrate exceptions into practical applications or recite an inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 — statutory category
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate Step 1: Does this claim fall within at least one statutory category?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the claim recites a statutory category (e.g., process, machine, manufacture, composition). Example: A non-transitory computer-readable storage medium is a "manufacture" and thus Step 1 = Yes because the BRI covers only statutory embodiments (not a transitory signal). If claim recites a series of steps, it may be a "process."

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2A Prong One — identify abstract idea / judicial exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate Step 2A Prong One: (a) identify the specific limitation(s) in the claim that you believe recite an abstract idea; and (b) determine whether the identified limitation(s) falls within at least one of the groupings of abstract ideas enumerated in MPEP 2106.04(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map claimed limitations to abstract-idea groupings (e.g., mathematical concepts, mental processes, laws of nature). Examples from the guidance: converting time-frequency representation into embeddings is a mathematical equation in prose; clustering with k-means is a mathematical calculation; applying binary masks is a mathematical calculation; comparing a PRS against top-quartile reference values is a mental process; describing genotype-phenotype relationships can implicate a law of nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2A Prong Two — additional elements and practical application
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate Step 2A Prong Two: (a) identify whether there are any additional elements recited in the claim beyond the judicial exception; and (b) evaluate those additional elements individually and in combination to determine whether the claim as a whole integrates the exception into a practical application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether additional elements meaningfully limit the abstract idea or show an improvement to technology/technical field. Elements that merely gather data or perform generic steps may be "insignificant extra-solution activity." By contrast, reciting specific technical steps or improvements (e.g., DNN-aided cluster assignments that are synthesized into time-domain waveforms and produce a technical improvement) can integrate the exception into a practical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2B — inventive concept (significantly more than the judicial exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate Step 2B: Does the claim provide an inventive concept, i.e., does the claim recite additional element(s) or a combination of elements that amount to significantly more than the judicial exception in the claim?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether additional elements (or their combination) add significantly more than the abstract idea. Mere instructions to apply the exception or insignificant extra-solution activity cannot provide an inventive concept. Example: a generic directive to administer an "appropriate treatment" does not supply an inventive concept; routine laboratory techniques (e.g., analyzing DNA to provide sequence information) are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insignificant extra-solution activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying elements that are merely extra-solution activity (insignificant to the practical application of the abstract idea).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples called out as insignificant: "transmitting" a signal, "receiving" mixed speech signal as mere data gathering, generic collection/genotyping when not claimed in a non-routine, specific way, and routine laboratory techniques (see MPEP 2106.05(d)). Such activities, by themselves, generally do not integrate an abstract idea into a practical application or supply an inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration into practical application — indicators of meaningful limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors that indicate a claim integrates the judicial exception into a practical application (i.e., meaningfully limits the abstract idea).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators include reciting technical improvements to computer technology or another technical field, reciting details of how a machine (e.g., a DNN) performs the claimed steps that produce a technical result, and using the exception to identify a specific population and implement a particular treatment tailored to that population (e.g., administering Compound X eye drops to glaucoma patients identified as high risk by PRS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadest reasonable interpretation (BRI) for claim construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the broadest reasonable interpretation in light of the specification to determine the scope of claim terms and embodiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret claim limitations in view of the specification; do not disregard limitations simply because they appear in a "wherein" clause — a wherein clause can have patentable weight. The BRI may distinguish between statutory and non-statutory embodiments (e.g., excluding transitory signals when the claim recites a non-transitory medium).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping limitations to abstract-idea groupings (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific examples of mapping claim limitations to abstract-idea groupings (mathematical concepts, mental processes, laws of nature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete mappings provided: converting a time-frequency representation into embeddings = mathematical concept; clustering embeddings with k-means = mathematical calculation; applying binary masks = mathematical calculation; extracting spectral features and generating words = processing leading to transcription (may involve abstract ideas); calculating a weighted polygenic risk score by multiplication and addition = mathematical calculation; comparing PRS to known thresholds = mental process; describing genotype-phenotype relationships = law of nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine implementation vs. mere use of computer as tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether invoking a machine or DNN transforms an abstract idea into a patent-eligible practical application, or merely uses a computer as a tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements like "using the DNN" can be merely instructions to implement an abstract idea on a computer (insufficient). However, reciting how the DNN materially aids cluster assignments and leads to a technical improvement (e.g., enabling separation without prior knowledge of speaker count, producing time-domain waveforms, enabling per-source transcription) may support eligibility by showing an integrated practical application or improvement to technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particularity/specific treatment can provide meaningful limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A dependent claim that adds particularity (specific treatment, drug, or technical step) can meaningfully limit the abstract idea and integrate it into a practical application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Claim 2 specifying that the "appropriate treatment is Compound X eye drops" was found to give the claim patentable weight where the particular treatment is tied to the identified patient population, and thus the abstract idea is used to deliver a particular treatment to a defined group.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fixed list; case-by-case analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no fixed list of terms that automatically render a claim eligible or ineligible; SME analysis is fact- and claim-specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2024 AI SME Update reiterates that USPTO guidance in MPEP Sections 2103–2106.07(c) applies across technologies and that the examples provided are illustrative; examiners and practitioners must evaluate every claim on a case-by-case basis.
